title: Coordination & Telemetry Gateway + Circuit Breaker Playbook
author: Leila Moreno
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes a coordinated runtime pattern we call the Coordination & Telemetry Gateway (CTG) and its paired Circuit Breaker (CB) policies. The goal is to provide a single control point for cross-cutting decisions (routing, degrade/fallback, and kernel-scheduling hints) while centralizing telemetry collection and defensive circuit-breaking for overload and kernel regressions.

Use cases:
- Protect downstream kernel pools from noisy/malicious traffic or sudden microbursts.
- Attach coherent telemetry and causal metadata to requests to enable rapid attribution during profiling and post-incident analysis.
- Provide safe, automated fallbacks (model variant, reduced tokens, synchronous->async) with audit trail.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted and Dedicated deployments; CTG is optional in Private but recommended as a light control-plane sidecar.
- Integrates with existing services: rt-gateway, kernel-scheduler, kv-cache-manager, telemetry-proxy, and the runtime orchestration plane.
- Assumes request metadata (route, token_count_estimate, customer_tier, affinity_tag) is available at ingress.

High-level architecture (text diagram):

Client -> rt-gateway -> CTG (coordination + telemetry-proxy) -> kernel-scheduler -> kernels (GPU pool)
                                   
CTG components:
- Ingress policy evaluator (rate limits, tenant priority, canary rules)
- Telemetry enrichment & sampler (adds request provenance, flags, and sampling decisions)
- Circuit-breaker engine (per-route/per-tenant, token/latency/error triggers)
- Kernel hint emitter (sends priority, batch_hint, prefetch_hint to kernel-scheduler)
- Fallback orchestrator (model variant & routing decisions; delegates to routing table)

Design goals and constraints:
- Deterministic decision surface: given identical request metadata, CTG must make repeatable routing and CB decisions.
- Low added latency: CTG target p95 additional latency < 1.5ms for simple passes; complex policy evaluation gated behind a fast-path.
- Observability-first: every circuit or fallback decision emits a standardized event with correlation_id and kernel_hint.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed: default behavior is fail-open for low-severity telemetry failures and fail-closed for security/policy violations.

Circuit Breaker Policy model:
- Dimensions: route, tenant, customer_tier, kernel_pool, model_variant.
- Signals: error_rate (5m/1m windows), tail_latency_p99, queue_length, kernel_backpressure_events, kvcache_miss_rate.
- Actions: reject, degrade (model_variant downgrade), throttle (token limit), route_to_dedicated_pool, switch-to-async, soft-fallback (shorter generation).

Default thresholds (operational baseline):
| Signal                        | Window | Threshold | Default action       |
|-------------------------------|--------|-----------|----------------------|
| error_rate                    | 1m     | 5%        | reject/route-to-dedicated_pool |
| tail_latency_p99              | 1m     | 2500ms    | degrade/throttle     |
| kernel_backpressure_events    | 5m     | 3 events  | route_to_dedicated_pool |
| queue_length (local)          | instant| 200      | switch-to-async      |
| kvcache_miss_rate             | 5m     | 30%       | prefetch, degrade    |

Policy lifecycle and rollout:
1. Author policy in git under infra/policies/ctg/*.yaml.
2. Unit test via policy-sim (synthetic signals).
3. Canary rollout to non-critical region (10% of traffic) for 24h.
4. Observe telemetry: decision_count, false_positive_rate (human triage), and recovery_time.
5. Gradual increase: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on safety triggers.

Kernel scheduling interactions:
- CTG emits kernel_hint: {priority: low/normal/high, batch_max_tokens, prefetch_keys, affinity_tag}.
- Scheduler maps kernel_hint.priority to slot buckets; high priority requests are eligible for preemption credits.
- When CTG sees repeated kernel_backpressure_events associated with a tenant, CB may route to a different kernel_pool or activate an economic-priority governor.
- Interaction contract: kernel-scheduler must accept hints within 2ms and provide an ack event back to CTG for tracing.

Profiling and telemetry integration:
- All CTG decisions annotate the trace with fields: ctg.decision, ctg.reason_code, ctg.policy_id, kernel_hint.*.
- Trace-sampling policy: 100% sampling for any request that triggered a CB action; 0.1% baseline sampling otherwise.
- Profiling playbook steps on a triggered CB:
  a) Tag all buffered traces with the CB window id.
  b) Reconstruct request-to-kernel timeline using trace_id and kernel_ack events.
  c) Run quick microprofile (sequence length / token distribution / kernel occupancy) and attach to incident.

Benchmark & acceptance checks before enabling CTG policies in production:
- Latency budget regression: enable CTG in passthrough mode and run mixed workload simulation (see benchmark: mixed_workload_slo_simulation_suite). Target: p50 change < 0.3ms, p95 change < 1.5ms.
- Decision correctness: inject synthetic signal scenarios and assert action matches policy in > 99% of cases.
- Observability completeness: events for decisions must include correlation_id, policy_id, and kernel_hint fields. Missing fields fail the gate.

Operational runbook (incident triage):
1. Detect: Alert triggered on ctg.circuit_opened.count > 5/min or ctg.degraded_routing.rate > 2% sustained for 3m.
2. Triage: Owner (runtime-ops) inspects last 100 ctg.events and related kernel_ack timelines.
3. Short-term mitigation (under 15m): temporarily set affected policy to "monitor-only" (no actions) via control-plane flag.
4. If root cause is kernel regression: route traffic away from kernel_pool (set policy action to route_to_dedicated_pool).
5. Follow-up: run profiling playbook, add new signal or adjust threshold, and schedule a policy change with a canary rollout.

Known issues and mitigations (catalog):
- Issue: CB oscillation when thresholds too tight for bursty tenants.
  Mitigation: add hysteresis (cooldown period 60s) and require cross-window confirmation.
- Issue: Telemetry-proxy packet loss causing missing kernel_ack events.
  Mitigation: enable TCP fallback for kernel-ack channel and raise sampling retention to avoid blind spots.
- Issue: High-cardinality tenant signals fill policy evaluation cache.
  Mitigation: cardinality cap per-policy (100 active keys) and LRU eviction with telemetry backoff.

Release checklist for CTG feature rollouts:
- Policy YAMLs validated and stored in git.
- Unit & integration tests pass in CI (policy-sim, rt-gateway integration).
- Perf benchmark: mixed-workload simulation within latency budget.
- Observability: dashboards created: CTG Decisions, CB opens, kernel_hint distribution.
- Runbook: on-call owner assigned and playbook published.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Primary: runtime-ops (oncall: runtime-ops rotation).
- Secondary: kernel-scheduling team (for hint contract).
- SLOs: CTG availability 99.95% (excludes planned rolling upgrades).
- Error budget consumption: any CTG-caused degradation that exceeds error budget requires rollback to passthrough within 2 hours.

Appendix: example policy fragment (YAML) and CLI examples:

Example policy (policy-id: tenant-burst-protect):
```yaml
policy_id: tenant-burst-protect
scope: tenant_id
triggers:
  - signal: queue_length
    window: instant
    threshold: 200
    action: switch-to-async
  - signal: kernel_backpressure_events
    window: 5m
    threshold: 2
    action: route_to_dedicated_pool
cooldown: 60s
```

CLI: temporarily set policy to monitor-only:
```bash
ctgctl set-policy --policy-id tenant-burst-protect --mode monitor-only --reason "triage temporary"
ctgctl status --policy-id tenant-burst-protect --last-24h
```

Telemetry fields (required for decision events):
- correlation_id (string)
- policy_id (string)
- ctg.decision (enum: allow, reject, degrade, route)
- ctg.reason_code (string)
- kernel_hint.priority (string)
- kernel_hint.batch_max_tokens (int)

Related improvements (roadmap):
- Adaptive thresholding using workload-aware baselines.
- Compact binary decision format for sub-ms fast-path evaluation.
- Per-tenant learning mode to auto-tune cooldown and hysteresis.
